newsitem.title: JAPAN: FREESTYLE SKIING-DOWNS FULFILS CHILDHOOD DREAM.
newsitem.headline: FREESTYLE SKIING-DOWNS FULFILS CHILDHOOD DREAM.

text.p: Canadian Darcy Downs fulfilled a childhood dream when he won the men's combined title at the world freestyle skiing championships on Thursday.
Downs, who missed most of last season with a shoulder injury, headed the four-man field with 30 points in acro, moguls and aerials.
Team mate Toben Sutherland was second with 27.6 and Oleg Kouleshov of Belarus third on 24.

"I got it into my head when I first started competing that I wanted to be world champion in combined," said 28-year-old Downs. "It was my dream from the start and I wanted to see it through to the end."
The tiny field the combined event attracted to the Mount Iizuna course on the outskirts of Nagano must cast doubts on its future in these championships. No women's combined has been scheduled.
With technical standards continually improving, most freestylers now specialise in one of the sports three disciplines to remain competitive.

The acceptance of moguls and aerials as Olympic events has also encouraged specialisation. The men's moguls event at the Iizuna ski area, where freestylers will return next year to compete in the Winter Olympics, attracted more then 40 entries.

"I hate to say it but there are fewer and fewer athletes getting involved in the combined," said Downs, who suggested that young skiers be introduced to all three disciplines when they first try the sport.
Downs said he would focus more on aerials himself during the coming Olympic year but would also continue competing in the gruelling three-day combined event.
